title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
why_read: A concrete, measurable defense against prompt injection attacks in LLMs, with clear benchmark comparisons against existing state-of-the-art methods.
analysis: Prompt injection, where malicious text embedded in data tricks a language model into following unintended instructions, is one of the most pressing unsolved security problems in deployed LLM systems. This paper proposes 'Heads of Security,' a lightweight modification that trains specific attention mechanisms to keep trusted instructions and untrusted data separate inside the model itself, rather than relying on external filtering. The reported numbers are striking: a strong attack that succeeds 97% of the time against an undefended model drops to only 10% success against this defense while preserving normal task performance. This is exactly the kind of practical, benchmarked security research that matters for anyone building LLM agents that process external content.
